LESSON: NON- METALLIC MATERIALS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Materials for Production
Topic 3.3: Non- Metallic Materials

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Non- Metallic Materials. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are non-metallic materials important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify non-metallic materials found in the locality
2. describe the physical properties of non-metallic materials found in the locality
3. appreciate the use of non- metallic materials in production

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: NON- METALLIC MATERIALS
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Non- Metallic Materials helps you succeed in PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

KEY FACTS: NON- METALLIC MATERIALS
Study Non- Metallic Materials like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify non-metallic materials found in the locality

What this means
In this part you learn to identify non-metallic materials found in the locality. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify non-metallic materials found in the locality.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Safety first: State one safety rule before practising “Non- Metallic Materials”.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify non-metallic materials found in the locality. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the physical properties of non-metallic materials found in the locality

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the physical properties of non-metallic materials found in the locality. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the physical properties of non-metallic materials found in the locality.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Steps: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Non- Metallic Materials.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the physical properties of non-metallic materials found in the locality. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the use of non- metallic materials in production

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the use of non- metallic materials in production. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the use of non- metallic materials in production.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Check: Inspect your work and say one improvement.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the use of non- metallic materials in production. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Non- Metallic Materials is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: State one safety rule before practising “Non- Metallic Materials”. (skill: identify non-metallic materials found in the locality)

Example 2: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Non- Metallic Materials. (skill: describe the physical properties of non-metallic materials found in the locality)

Example 3: Inspect your work and say one improvement. (skill: appreciate the use of non- metallic materials in production)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Non- Metallic Materials to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify non-metallic materials found in the locality.
3. Practise this skill: describe the physical properties of non-metallic materials found in the locality.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the use of non- metallic materials in production.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Non- Metallic Materials from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Non- Metallic Materials: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Non- Metallic Materials?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are non-metallic materials important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Non- Metallic Materials means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify non-metallic materials found in the locality.
5. Be able to: describe the physical properties of non-metallic materials found in the locality.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
